resources.string: In the Spaces tab, you can create a limited palette by defining three primary colors and choosing a mixing style: additive or subtractive.
Choose Primaries: Press and hold a highlighted hex to change its color.
The hex grid updates automatically to display the resulting color blends.
Click any hex to store its color in the bottom bar for easy reference.
You can save up to 10 personalized palettes and switch between them using the buttons above the grid.
Additive Mixing: Use darker primaries, as lighter ones can be too overwhelming.
Subtractive Mixing: Use lighter primaries, as darker ones may overpower the palette.
The Lights tab lets you explore how different colored materials react under various lighting conditions.
Change the Sphere’s Color: Click the button below the sphere.
Adjust Light Colors: Tap the left or right lightbulb icons to select their colors.
Turn Off the Right Light: Use the switch to disable the right light source.
Pick Colors from the Sphere: Click anywhere on the sphere to get the exact color at that point.
The simulation is based on RGB light sources, meaning results may differ from monochromatic light.
The final color of the sphere depends on how light interacts with its surface, helping you understand **light diffusion and material behavior**.
The Guess tab is a Wordle-like game where you have six tries to guess the hex code of the displayed color.
Each row represents a guess with three cells: Red (R), Green (G), and Blue (B).
Type two hexadecimal characters (00 to FF) into each cell to form a color guess.
When you finish a row, it is automatically submitted, and feedback is provided.
🔵 Blue Cell: Too low, increase this value.
🔴 Red Cell: Too high, decrease this value.
🎉 If you correctly guess the color, you win!
❌ If you don’t guess it in six attempts, the correct hex code is revealed.

This app was created from my personal journey into color theory. Initially, I started studying colors to improve my drawing skills, but I quickly became fascinated by how colors interact, blend, and influence perception.
I wanted to build a tool to help visual artists, designers, and anyone interested in color theory experiment with color relationships in an intuitive way.
It was also an opportunity to improve my Android development skills by applying modern concepts like Jetpack Compose, MVVM architecture, and data persistence.
🎨 Spaces Tab: Create custom palettes by mixing colors in additive or subtractive modes.
💡 Lights Tab: Experiment with how different light sources affect materials and colors.
🎯 Guess Tab: Play a Wordle-like game to sharpen your ability to recognize and work with color hex codes.
